title: Build the browser attachment service with createRemoteAttachmentService from @powerhousedao/reactor-attachments/client
content:
## The import that matters

```ts
import { createRemoteAttachmentService } from "@powerhousedao/reactor-attachments/client";
```

Point it at the same Switchboard the light client uses, then pass it in:

```tsx
<GraphQLReactorProvider url={switchboardUrl} attachmentService={attachmentService}>
  <YourApp />
</GraphQLReactorProvider>
```

Import the **`/client` subpath, not the package root**. The root entry also exports the Kysely, S3 and filesystem backends, so a browser bundler has to resolve `kysely`, `@aws-sdk/client-s3` and `node:fs` — and fails before any app code runs. This is the same failure class as importing `@powerhousedao/reactor-browser` from its root instead of `/graphql-client`, and it has the same shape of fix: import the browser subpath.

## Who owns what

Attachments are configured at the same point as everything else, but the **app constructs the service**. Which storage it talks to is the app's business; `@powerhousedao/reactor-browser` does not depend on the attachment implementation at all.

The provider publishes the service into the `window.ph.attachmentService` slot Connect publishes it into, so `useAttachmentService` and the editors below find it. Leave the prop out and the slot stays empty, exactly as it is without the provider.

It is published from its **own effect, keyed on the prop**, so an app that builds the service asynchronously can pass it in later — passing a new service does not rebuild the client or the document cache.

## Honest caveat

The docs are explicit that this prop is a **wiring seam and nothing more has been proven**: the service an app passes reaches `useAttachmentService` below the provider, but no attachment has been read over the light client end to end. Treat a working attachment flow on this client as something to verify yourself rather than assume.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/04-Reference/08-ReactorBrowserClient/03-SubgraphsAndAttachments.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
description: The package root also exports the Kysely, S3 and filesystem backends, so only the /client subpath is browser-safe.
